name: Stoicism
line: Live by reason. Accept what is not up to you.
era: c. 300 BCE to 180 CE, revived today

quote.text: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of them.

words.meaning: The reason that orders the world

rules.text: Pause before reacting. Name the judgment.

ethics.title: Virtue is the only good
ethics.text: Wisdom, justice, courage and moderation. Everything else is preferred or not, never good or bad.

ethics.title: We are made for each other
ethics.text: Marcus: like hands, feet and eyelids, we exist to cooperate.

ethics.title: Accept what you cannot change
ethics.text: Meet fate with a steady mind and do your part.

philosophy.title: The dichotomy of control
philosophy.text: Some things are up to you: judgment, intention, action. The rest is not.

philosophy.title: The view from above
philosophy.text: Imagine your life from far overhead. Most troubles shrink.

philosophy.title: Premeditation of evils
philosophy.text: Rehearse what could go wrong so it cannot surprise you.

journal: What disturbed you today: the event, or your judgment of it?
What was up to you today, and what was not?
Where did you act from virtue, even in a small way?
What obstacle did you expect, and how did it go?
Who did you treat unjustly or coldly? What would repair it?
What would you do today if it were your last?
What did you want that you do not need?
reflect: What did you control this Onda, and what did you only think you controlled?
Which practice changed you the most, and why?
Where did you resist, and what was the resistance protecting?

intro: Stoicism is a practical philosophy of life. It teaches that we suffer less from events than from the judgments we add to them, and that a good character is enough for a good life.
It began in a painted porch in Athens, grew through Rome, and sat close to emperors and slaves alike. Its lessons are exercises: things to practice, not theories to admire.
guide.era: c. 300 BCE to 180 CE, revived today

figures.name: Zeno of Citium
figures.bio: Founder. Taught at the Stoa Poikile, the painted porch that gave the school its name.

figures.name: Seneca
figures.bio: Roman statesman and playwright. Wrote letters on how to live.

figures.name: Epictetus
figures.bio: Born a slave. Taught that freedom lives in your own choices.

figures.name: Marcus Aurelius
figures.bio: Roman emperor. His private notes became the Meditations.

history.what: Zeno begins teaching at the Stoa Poikile in Athens
history.detail: The school took its name from the porch, stoa in Greek.

history.what: Chrysippus systematizes Stoic logic and ethics
Seneca and Musonius Rufus carry Stoicism through Rome
Epictetus teaches; his student Arrian records the Discourses
Marcus Aurelius writes the Meditations on campaign

concepts.text: Moral excellence, the one thing fully in your control.
Health, wealth and reputation. Preferred, but never the point.
Impressions arrive uninvited. What you agree to is your choice.
All things are connected in one living whole.

facts.text: Epictetus was lame, and by tradition his leg was broken by his master.
Marcus Aurelius never meant the Meditations to be published. The title is not his.
The word stoic comes from the painted porch where Zeno taught.
